title: Terrible Thought! Shall I Alone
description: Terrible Thought! Shall I Alone in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 80.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ter-ri-ble thought! shall I a-lone, Who may be saved shall I Of all, a-las! whom I have known, Through sin for ev-er die?

lines: Terrible thought! shall I alone,
Who may be saved shall I
Of all, alas! whom I have known,
Through sin for ever die?
While all my old companions dear,
With whom I once did live,
Joyful at God's right hand appear,
A blessing to receive;
Shall I - amidst a ghastly band,
Dragged to the judgment-seat -
Far on the left with horror stand,
My fearful doom to meet?
Ah, no! I still may turn and live,
For still his wrath delays;
He now vouchsafes a kind reprieve,
And offers me his grace.
I will accept his offers now,
From every sin depart,
Perform my oft-repeated vow
And render him my heart.
I will improve what I receive,
The grace through Jesus given;
Sure, if with God on earth I live,
To live with him in heaven.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
